question.problem:
The center of the hyperbola $-{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-32y-8x=16$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of a vertical hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the equation of the hyperbola in the above form, we need to group $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{x}^{2}+16{y}^{2}-32y-8x & =16 \\ 16{y}^{2}-32y-{x}^{2}-8x & =16 \\ 16[{y}^{2}-2y]-[{x}^{2}+8x] & =16 \\ 16[(y-1)^{2}-1]-[(x+4)^{2}-16] & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-16-(x+4)^{2}+16 & =16 \\ 16(y-1)^{2}-(x+4)^{2} & =16 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x+4)^{2}}{16} & =1 \\ \frac{(y-1)^{2}}{1}-\frac{(x-(-4))^{2}}{16} & =1\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,-4,1\,).$
